Snippet.Description:
Completed in 1892, Carl Nielsen's Symphony No. 1 premiered on March 14, 1894, at Copenhagen's Theatre Royal with Nielsen himself playing among the second violins, and the audience received it with excited applause. The work unfolds in four bold and adventurous movements: the dramatically insistent "Allegro orgoglioso" (spirited and proud), a profoundly moving "Andante," an unconventional third movement in the complex 6/4 time signature, and a finale that begins and ends in C major despite its G minor key signature.

Music Director Thomas Søndergård led the Minnesota Orchestra in this performance on January 10, 2026.
Snippet.Title: Nielsen's Symphony No. 1 | Minnesota Orchestra | Thomas Søndergård

Snippet.Description:
Hector Berlioz's revolutionary Symphonie fantastique (1830), written just three years after Beethoven's death, transformed the symphony into an autobiographical narrative inspired by the composer's obsessive love for actress Harriet Smithson. The work follows an artist who poisons himself with opium after unrequited love, experiencing vivid hallucinations traced through five movements: from the introduction of the beloved's musical theme (the "idée fixe") in "Reveries–Passions," through a glittering waltz at "A Ball" and pastoral anxieties "In the Country," to the nightmarish "March to the Scaffold" where he dreams of his own execution, culminating in the grotesque "Dream of the Witches' Sabbath" where his beloved appears as a trivial dance tune amid sorcerers and devils. This performance features a pair of large church bells custom-cast for the Minnesota Orchestra by the Royal Eijsbouts foundry in the Netherlands, donated by patron Gary B. Cohen and now part of the Orchestra's permanent collection.

Conductor Thomas Søndergård led the Minnesota Orchestra in this performance on November 14, 2025.
Snippet.Title: Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique | Minnesota Orchestra | Thomas Søndergård

Snippet.Description:
Immerse yourself in an orchestral experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat as Thomas Søndergård conducts Stravinsky’s groundbreaking and radical ballet score The Rite of Spring. Lili Boulanger’s Of a Spring Morning brings a sweet, playful beginning to this program that truly puts the entire ensemble at the center. In between, and also orchestrated for dance, Ravel’s Mother Goose ballet includes five tender and nostalgic miniatures inspired by fairy tales.

This concert was recorded live at Orchestra Hall on October 21, 2022 as part of the series, "This Is Minnesota Orchestra."
Snippet.Title: Søndergård Conducts Rite of Spring: Full Concert | This Is Minnesota Orchestra

Snippet.Description:
Jean Sibelius' Violin Concerto had a troubled birth: the 1904 Helsinki premiere featured an inadequately prepared soloist and received mostly negative reviews, prompting Sibelius to revise the work extensively before its successful 1905 Berlin premiere with Richard Strauss conducting. The composer's affinity for the violin stemmed from his youthful aspiration to become a great violinist, and though he began training too late for a performance career, he poured that passion into this concerto's fiendishly difficult solo part. The work features dark, somber orchestral colors and original formal structures: the first movement eschews traditional development in favor of elaborating each theme upon presentation, the Adagio contrasts dreamy reflection with turbulent passion, and the energetic finale in rondo form evokes polonaise and Romani dance rhythms while demanding the soloist's full technical prowess.

Music Director Thomas Søndergård led the Minnesota Orchestra with soloist James Ehnes in this performance on January 10, 2026.
Snippet.Title: James Ehnes Plays Sibelius' Violin Concerto | Minnesota Orchestra | Thomas Søndergård
